'''Jonas Harold Ellenberg''' is [[emeritus]] professor of [[biostatistics]] and [[epidemiology]] in the Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology & Informatics of the [[Perelman School of Medicine]], [[University of Pennsylvania]]. He is a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], the [[Society for Clinical Trials]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).

==Education==
Ellenberg earned his BSc{{efn|Sources are divided regarding his major at Wharton. He studied either economics{{r|AmStatNews2016}} or statistics.{{r|AmStatNews2013}}}} from the [[Wharton School]] at the University of Pennsylvania in 1963 and his AM and PhD (both in [[mathematical statistics]]) from [[Harvard University]] in 1964 and 1970, respectively. His PhD thesis, ''Detection of Outliers in Multivariate Linear Regression,'' was written under the tutelage of [[William Gemmell Cochran|W. G. Cochran]].{{r|AmStatNews2016|AmStatNews2013|MathGenealogy}}

==Career==
After completion of his PhD, Ellenberg joined the National Institute for Neurological Diseases and Blindness (now known as the National Institute for Neurological Diseases and Stroke [NINDS]) at the [[National Institutes of Health]], where he studied the causes of neurologic disorders in children, including [[cerebral palsy]] (CP) and [[febrile seizure]] from the [[Collaborative Perinatal Project]]. Results from this large [[longitudinal study]] showed for the first time that CP was partially caused by factors occurring before labor and delivery. Ellenberg's collaboration with medical researchers also demonstrated that use of [[phenobarbital]] did not prevent repeat febrile seizures in infants.{{r|AmStatNews2016|Kolata1990}} Ellenberg stayed at NINDS for 26 years, including 11 years as head of the biometrics department.{{r|AmStatNews2016}}

After leaving NIH, Ellenberg joined [[Westat]] as vice president and head of biostatistics, where he remained for 10 years.{{r|AmStatNews2013}}

In 2004, Ellenberg became professor of biostatistics and associate dean of the school of medicine at the University of Pennsylvania.{{r|AmStatNews2016}}

==Recognition==
Ellenberg was elected as a [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|fellow of the ASA]] in 1982{{r|ASAFellows}}, the Society for Clinical Trials in 2014{{r|SCTFellows}}, and the AAAS in 1994{{r|AAASFellows}}. He was an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]]. In 1988, he served as president of the International Biometric Society{{r|IBSPrez}}, and in 1999 became the [[List of presidents of the American Statistical Association|president of the ASA]].{{r|AmStatNews2016}}

==Personal life==
Ellenberg is the husband of statistician [[Susan S. Ellenberg]]{{r|AmStatNews2013}} and father of mathematician [[Jordan Ellenberg]]{{r|Nadis2021}}
